<MethodEndpoint
  method={"post"}
  path={"/standards"}
  context={"endpoint"}
>
  
</MethodEndpoint>



If a standard is already active for this TaskType, it is closed (its effective range ends now) and a new one starts — append-only history, never an in-place overwrite.

A standard may optionally be declared for one handling unit (`handlingUnit`: EACH, CASE or PALLET), so a case handle has its own expected time distinct from an each pick. At most one standard is open per (taskType, handlingUnit): defining a CASE standard never closes the task-type-only one, and revising it closes only the prior CASE standard. A CASE standard may also declare a heavy-case `teamLift` (ADR 0035).

A standard may optionally be scoped to one site (`siteCode`, a facility-layout site code, ADR 0038). Absent means the site-less standard that applies to every site, exactly as before. At most one standard is open per (taskType, handlingUnit, siteCode): a site's standard never closes the site-less one, nor the reverse, and revising it closes only the prior standard of the same site. Scoring is unchanged: completed tasks are still scored against site-less standards only.

Idempotent retries: clients MUST always send an `Idempotency-Key` header (1-128 printable ASCII characters, a client-generated UUID per logical submit); a retried request with the same key, method, path and body replays the original response byte-for-byte, with the response header `Idempotency-Replayed: true`, instead of defining the standard a second time. The same key with a different method, path or body is 409 `idempotency-key-reused`.

What is replayed: a 2xx, and a refusal that is final for the request (a validation answer such as 400 `unknown-task-type` or 422 `non-positive-expected-seconds`). A refusal that depends on state that can change is NOT stored and its key is released, so the same request under the same key executes again: 409 `concurrent-modification` and 409 `standard-conflict`, and every 5xx or panic. A different body under a released key is a new request.
